elements.element: Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor.
elements.evidence: Revised Section 7.2 reads: "Customer has no obligation to disclose or match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives from another provider." The disclose-and-match obligation running to Vendor is eliminated, and no other provision imposes a most-favoured-customer or price-matching duty on Customer; Section 12.3 is retained and now consistent ("Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no ... most-favoured-customer ... commitment").

elements.element: The Customer MFN covers only a defined product.
elements.evidence: Conditional element: it presupposes a surviving Customer MFN. After the edit no Customer MFN obligation remains anywhere in the operative text (Section 7.2 is an express negation; Section 12.3 disclaims any most-favoured-customer commitment), so the product-scope limit has nothing to bind and the condition does not apply.

elements.element: The Customer MFN lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Conditional element: no Customer MFN survives the redline, so there is no term to cap. Section 7.2 as rendered imposes no disclosure or matching duty for any period.

elements.element: The Customer MFN contains reasonable like-for-like comparison carve-outs.
elements.evidence: Conditional element: with the matching obligation deleted there is no comparison mechanic requiring carve-outs; nothing in the rendered language obliges Customer to benchmark third-party offers against Vendor terms.

reasons: The single operation targets exactly the offending obligation in Section 7.2 and converts it into an express negation; no survival tail, expense allocation, procedure, or unrelated boilerplate was added, and no other clause was touched.

Section 12.3 — which is favourable to Customer and independently confirms no most-favoured-customer commitment — is retained verbatim, so no Customer-favourable language was stripped and the previously contradictory pairing of 7.2 and 12.3 is resolved.
No Vendor-granted MFN exists in the document, so the redline does not disturb any pricing benefit running in Customer's favour, consistent with the rule's instruction to keep any Vendor-granted MFN.

The rewrite leaves no undefined term or dangling cross-reference: Section 7.2 keeps its number and remains a complete sentence, and no other provision cross-references the deleted disclose-and-match mechanic.
Fallback elements are recorded as met only vacuously — their condition (a surviving Customer MFN) no longer applies. Completion here rests on the preferred level, which is fully achieved.

Drafting note (no defect): the negation form is slightly more verbose than a clean deletion of Section 7.2, but it is not an extra requirement and it usefully forecloses any argument that a residual matching duty survives.
